etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English tune, an unexplained variant of tone, from Old French ton, from Latin tonus, from Ancient Greek τόνος (tónos, “a tone”). Doublet of tone, ton, and tonus.

definitions.definition: A song, or short musical composition.
(informal) The act of tuning or maintenance.
The state or condition of being correctly tuned.
(obsolete) A sound; a note; a tone.

definitions.definition: (UK, slang) Used to show appreciation or approval of a song.

definitions.definition: To adjust or modify (especially a mechanical or electrical device) so that it functions optimally.
To adjust the frequency on a radio or TV set, so as to receive the desired channel.
Of faculties, senses, etc.: to adapt to or direct towards a particular target.
To make more precise, intense, or effective; to put into a proper state or disposition.
